commands.name: init
commands.title: wsync init
commands.description: Initializes a directory as a WSync project from a template and writes the project file, agent context, and local Luau tooling files without starting a daemon.
notes: Templates are `place`, `quick`, `model`, `package`, `plugin`, and `empty`. They ship embedded, install to `~/.wsync/templates/`, and are versioned and refreshed by `wsync update templates`.

Writes default.project.json plus agent docs (a concise AGENTS.md contract linking the detailed wsync.md reference, CLAUDE.md import, and .codex/config.toml). Existing user notes are preserved by guarded writers.
Project names and Roblox identity fields belong in the generated .project.json config. `--git`, `--wally`, `--selene`, `--docs`, `--license`, and `--ts` control scaffolding.
An existing project is retained and init asks before adding missing template files. No legacy migration or identity flags are implied.
This command never starts a daemon.

commands.name: plugin
commands.title: wsync plugin
commands.description: Installs or removes a local WSync Studio plugin file.
notes: Default mode is install. The optional second positional argument is the destination file or directory, not a source plugin.

Installation searches plugin/WSync.rbxm relative to the working directory, then WSync.rbxm next to the CLI binary, then the binary-embedded plugin. If no source exists it returns an error; this command does not download one.
With no destination, Roblox Studio installation discovery chooses the local plugins directory. Directory destinations receive WSync.rbxm; smart_paths also interprets extensionless destinations.
Install creates destination parent directories and writes the plugin file. Uninstall removes that selected file and returns a filesystem error if it is absent.

No status subcommand or --raw/--source/--plugin-dir flags are implemented. Use the destination positional argument for a custom install location. Reload plugins or restart Studio to load a changed plugin file.

commands.name: auth
commands.title: wsync auth
commands.description: Stores, inspects, or clears the CLI Roblox Open Cloud credential and named per-account profiles without accepting or printing a secret as a command-line value.
examples: printf '%s' "$OWNER_KEY" | wsync auth set --from-stdin --profile owner --creator user:123456 --raw
notes: `auth set` requires exactly one of `--from-stdin`, `--file`, or `--from-env`; the credential itself is never accepted in argv and is never logged.
Secrets resolve to the OS keychain first. The CLI fallback store uses a private per-user data directory with mode 0600 on Unix; it is filesystem-permission protected, not an OS keychain.
`upload` and `monetization` discover this store before falling back to `--api-key-env` and then to the `ROBLOX_API_KEY`, `CLOUD_API_KEY`, and `ROBLOX_OPEN_CLOUD_API_KEY` environment variables.

`--profile <name>` stores a named profile (one per Roblox account or group) holding its own key, a default `--creator`, or both; `--creator` alone makes a profile that switches only the creator and borrows the normal credential chain. `status` lists every profile with masked key tails. `upload` and `monetization` select one with `--profile` or `WSYNC_PROFILE`.

commands.name: branch
commands.title: wsync branch
commands.description: Creates, lists, reopens, closes and merges branches: a git worktree, its own daemon, a Studio on an immutable clone of the place, and the journal of what that Studio changed.
notes: A branch is four things: the git worktree .wsync-branches/<name>/tree on branch wsync/<name>, a daemon started on that worktree, a Studio opened on the immutable clone .wsync-branches/<name>/<name>.rbxl, and the journal that clone's plugin pushes to its daemon. The record .wsync-branches/<name>/branch.json describes all four.

New takes the checkpoint from main's Studio, downloads one blob per service, assembles the clone with a ServerStorage/WSyncBranch marker, writes the worktree's project file with initialSync disk and a synthetic placeId derived from the name, starts the branch daemon, launches Studio, and has the branch plugin adopt main's numbering. The counts are not expected to match, because Studio adds instances of its own as it opens a place file: the checkpoint also carries a compact shape of the numbered tree, which travels to the branch daemon and lets adopt align by name and class. A clone the shape cannot be aligned against is refused, with what it matched and what was extra or missing.
The clone is immutable and the journal is the state, so up reopens the clone, adopts the numbering again and replays the branch's own journal into its own Studio. Nothing is rewritten on autosave.

Finish commits the worktree, then commits exactly the files main has changed that the branch also touched (the daemon regenerates the agent docs on every plugin connect, which would otherwise make git refuse the merge outright); unrelated changes in main are left alone and counted. It then runs git merge --no-ff --no-commit in the main checkout, flushes the branch journal, pauses main's sync, and replays the events into main's Studio. Git conflicts and replay conflicts both stop the merge and exit 3; replay conflicts are parked in .wsync-branches/<name>/conflicts.json.

Pick writes .wsync-branches/<name>/decisions.json; ours keeps main's value, theirs takes the branch's. Run branch finish again to apply the rest: that rerun resumes the merge git already has in progress instead of starting another, skipping the parking commit that git would reject as a partial commit mid-merge. A merge someone already committed is treated as done, not as a failure, and both files are cleared once the branch is finished.

A merge is not committed when the replay stopped early or had to skip an added subtree whose bytes exist nowhere any more; the git merge stays in progress and a rerun resumes it, the plugin's per-checkpoint ledger skipping what already landed. Before a subtree is called lost, finish asks the live branch Studio to serialize the instance again (journal_recapture), because its pinned copy expires ten minutes after the daemon last touched it and a daemon that was down or restarted never pulled it; a branch daemon that is not answering is started again first. The replay itself goes over in chunks of 250 events so no single call outlasts the daemon's heartbeat. --allow-missing-blobs commits anyway, for subtrees carried over by hand; the wsync-branch-recovery skill is the manual ladder for everything the rerun does not clear.

The merge commit is scoped to git diff --name-only HEAD...MERGE_HEAD plus the conflicted paths. The branch directory is never added, and the main checkout's sync is resumed whether the replay succeeded or failed. Main's own project file is restored from HEAD before the commit, so a merge never hands main the branch's name, branch field or synthetic place ID. WSync does not request a programmatic place save. Branch state is preserved by the serialized clone and journal until explicitly purged; save merged instance changes through main Studio's native save controls when needed.

Rm stops the Studio and the daemon and keeps the worktree, the clone and the journal. --purge also removes the worktree, deletes the branch wsync/<name> and the directory, and refuses a dirty worktree unless --force.

One owner per branch is recorded in branch.json. A branch whose owner process is gone is adopted by the next command; a branch whose owner is still running is refused unless --steal. At most three branch Studios are live at once (--budget overrides), because past Roblox's window cap a launch succeeds into a windowless stub; a refusal names branch rm.
Every subcommand runs from the main checkout. Running inside a branch worktree is refused: a branch of a branch has no checkpoint to fork from.

Scripts are not in the journal. WSync writes every script to disk as it changes, so a branch's script work is its worktree and finish merges it with git; the Studio replay skips file-backed script sources.

commands.name: daemon
commands.title: wsync daemon
commands.description: Starts, inspects, stops, restarts or reads logs from a project-scoped daemon with a lifecycle record.
notes: Start and restart serve in the current process; they do not detach into a background child. A process manager can launch them as a background service. --raw emits a readiness JSON line and then the process continues serving.
Start accepts --project, --port, --managed-by, --owner-token-env, --data-dir, --game-id, --group-id, repeated --place-id and --raw. Metadata flags persist those IDs into the project before startup.

Restart accepts --project, --port, --managed-by, --owner-token-env, --data-dir, --timeout and --raw. It uses persisted project metadata and does not accept game/group/place ID flags. The timeout is the wait for the old daemon to stop.

Status accepts --project, --data-dir and --raw; --raw also reports `route` (the project's URL on the hub) and `routed` (whether the hub reaches this exact boot). Stop also accepts --timeout. Logs accepts --project, --data-dir and --lines; it prints text lines without a --raw mode.

A matching daemon already running for the project is reported instead of starting a duplicate; with --raw the answer carries `routed`, and a daemon the hub does not reach (one from an older build) has to be restarted. Without --port or a project-file `port`, the daemon binds whatever port the OS hands out. A pinned port that is taken or serving another project is an error — nothing scans for another. Restart does not keep the previous port; the project's hub route is what stays the same, so a connected Studio reconnects on its own.

Every daemon registers with the WSync hub on 127.0.0.1:7960 (`WSYNC_HUB_PORT` overrides) over a WebSocket it holds open, and starts the hub when none answers; the hub exits a minute after its last registration closes. Everything reaches the daemon at `http://127.0.0.1:7960/p/<route>`, where the route is the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the canonical project path. --port only pins the daemon's own port, for a client that cannot use a route, such as a stock Argon plugin.

Stop verifies the exact live canonical project and boot ID before graceful shutdown. On graceful timeout it can use an OS-kill fallback only for that verified process; a stale PID record alone is insufficient.
Runtime records live in the platform data directory under WSync/daemons, alongside start locks and lifecycle logs. The mutation audit log is WSync/writes.log.
Desktop managers can supply an owner token through --owner-token-env <ENV>. Lifecycle JSON does not disclose the token. No --projects-root flag is implemented in this CLI family.

commands.name: commands
commands.title: wsync commands
commands.description: Prints generated command docs as JSON, either as a compact LLM index, one command entry, or the full registry.
notes: Defaults to a compact offline index; --compact remains an alias for index mode. --full explicitly prints the complete embedded registry.
Focused command lookup accepts nested paths and reports current parser help plus exact subcommand effects. --project is accepted for consistency and never causes discovery to connect to Studio.
`wsync commands types [TypeName]` provides offline JSON value schemas, field names, constraints and examples. Type lookup is case-insensitive.
The compact index includes CLI version, build commit/dirty identity, schema version and SHA-256 fingerprints of the embedded command and value catalogs. No network is required.

commands.name: context
commands.title: wsync context
commands.description: Prints a compact LLM-oriented project context snapshot as JSON.
notes: Reads project and daemon state without mutation or backlog cleanup. Missing live facts are null/unknown, not zero.
Includes canonical project identity, synced roots, generated-file presence, instruction-size warning, daemon/project match, plugin status, read-only backlog count and schema/build fingerprints.

The daemon is reached through the project's route on the WSync hub unless --port names a daemon's own port. `daemon.address` is the base URL used, `daemon.port` the port the daemon itself reports, and `daemon.portSource` says how it was chosen (`hub`, `--port` or `--place`).

Fetch when necessary project/connection facts are missing or stale. Refresh after project switches, reconnects, daemon restarts, binary upgrades or configuration changes. Reuse a successful snapshot during ordinary work.

Includes focused command/value-schema pointers and a concise llmPolicy: retain user authorization, coordinate one Studio lifecycle owner, avoid guessing value schemas, and check partial/unknown writes before retrying.
Use --full-commands only when the complete registry is needed; --raw returns a single JSON line.

commands.name: capabilities
commands.title: wsync capabilities
commands.description: Negotiates the connected daemon, Studio plugin, host DataModel, and optional LLM automation features before an agent chooses a command path.
notes: The `wsync/1` capability document reports the daemon and plugin build identity plus feature flags for exact physical-path identity, stats-first bounded per-root bootstrap with daemon-authored identity receipts, selective initial disk-to-Studio sync, native instance clipboard copy/paste, permission-free internal RGBA capture, playtesting, runtime execution, virtual input, UI inspection, artifacts, and workflows. `features.instanceClipboard` advertises `wsync copy`/`paste`; capture limits describe the unified `ui`, `model`, and `viewport` renderer.
Use this cheap read before relying on optional Studio APIs; Studio version and permission differences are reported instead of guessed.
Protocol and capability mismatches are negotiated at the WebSocket hello, so an incompatible plugin is reported here rather than failing mid-command.
`--raw` prints the complete correlated response envelope for machine use.

commands.name: capture
commands.title: wsync capture
commands.description: Captures transparent UI, a model or scene, or the current 3D viewport through WSync's permission-free internal renderer. Every command writes a locally encoded and verified PNG without placing image bytes on stdout.
commands.usage: wsync capture <ui|model|viewport> [TARGET] [--project <path>] [--port <port>] [--size WxH] [--region x,y,w,h] [--view <preset>] [--direction x,y,z] [--camera-cframe <12 floats>] [--padding 1.0-4.0] [--fov 1-120] [--world] [--skybox] [--framed] [--ui none|overlay] [-o|--output <file>] [--timeout <seconds>] [--raw]
notes: All three capture commands use the packaged internal RGBA renderer. They never request Roblox Studio screenshot permission, macOS Screen Recording permission, or a place-provided capture dependency.

`capture ui [TARGET]` captures only edit-mode ScreenGui pixels on a transparent background and never includes the 3D world or Studio chrome. TARGET is an optional ScreenGui or GuiObject path; when supplied, unrelated UI is hidden and the rendered target is tight-cropped before it is aspect-contained in `--size`. `--region x,y,width,height` selects an explicit rectangle in native viewport pixels.

`capture model TARGET` clones the target without scripts, isolates it, removes the skybox, and tight-crops its rendered alpha by default. `--world` frames the original target in place. `--skybox` keeps the world background and produces an opaque scene capture. `--framed` keeps the complete camera-framed canvas instead of applying the default subject-alpha crop.

For model captures, `--view` accepts isometric, front, back, left, right, top, or bottom; `--direction x,y,z` overrides it. `--camera-cframe` accepts exactly the 12 finite values returned by `CFrame:GetComponents()` and replaces automatic view, direction, and padding framing. `--padding` is 1.0-4.0 and `--fov` is 1-120 degrees.

`capture viewport` captures the complete current 3D viewport. It defaults to a transparent world with no in-game UI; `--skybox` preserves the rendered sky and world background, while `--ui overlay` includes visible ScreenGui layers over the scene. `--region x,y,width,height` selects an explicit rectangle in native viewport pixels.

For every no-skybox capture, WSync temporarily moves every `Sky` and `Atmosphere` descendant out from under `Lighting` before rendering and watches for matching descendants added while capture is active. Cleanup restores each object to its exact original parent—even after preparation, rendering, transport, or PNG failure—and falls back to `Lighting` only if that parent disappeared. Camera, UI, Lighting properties, and temporary clones receive the same protected cleanup.

`--size WIDTHxHEIGHT` is optional and requests exact output dimensions. Without it, model captures use the focused-render default of 1024x1024 while UI and viewport captures keep their native/current render dimensions. `--output`/`-o`, `--timeout`, and `--raw` are common to every capture type; default files are `wsync-ui.png`, `wsync-model.png`, and `wsync-viewport.png`. Each axis is limited to 4096 pixels and the image to 16777216 pixels.

The plugin sends tightly packed RGBA8 in bounded chunks. The CLI checks dimensions, exact byte length, offsets, and EOF, then encodes and verifies the PNG locally. Raw output includes the absolute output path, MIME type, byte size, dimensions, SHA-256, and prepared capture metadata without placing pixels on stdout.
Negative camera vectors and CFrame components are accepted as separate option values, for example --direction -1,0,0. The equals form --direction=-1,0,0 works too.

commands.name: playtest
commands.title: wsync playtest
commands.description: Runs playscript-owned foreground sessions, records screenshots and video clips from a live playtest, and controls lower-level asynchronous Studio playtests and isolated PlayServer and PlayClient runtime agents.
notes: `run --script <file>` owns the complete foreground lifecycle: it starts a Studio playtest, waits for the selected `--context` (`server` by default), injects the playscript, streams progress, prints the return value, and stops the playtest without another WSync invocation.

Run flags are `--script`, `--context server|client:N`, optional `--client-script`, `--mode play|run|multiplayer`, `--players` (1-8), JSON `--args`, `--timeout` (600 seconds by default, maximum 3600), `--identity game|plugin`, `--logs off|info|warn|error`, `--capture-dir` (`wsync-captures` by default), `--keep-open`, `--quiet`, and `--raw`. Invalid JSON is rejected before a job starts.

The injected API exposes `playtest.args`, `mode`, `context`, and `jobId`; `emit(data)` and `log(msg)` stream progress; `done(value)` and `fail(msg)` complete from any task; `capture(name)` and `clip(seconds, name)` record the viewport from a client context; and generation-scoped `signal`, `await`, and server-only `awaitClients` coordinate contexts.

The first completion wins. Main return or `done` exits 0; a main-script error or `fail` exits 2; hard timeout exits 3; an externally ended job exits 4 with its fetched `jobStatus`; and boot or required-context failure exits 5. Runs stop automatically except with `--keep-open`, which prints the job ID for later `exec`, `logs`, `capture`, and `stop` use.

`--client-script` runs once in every client as it becomes ready. Each return is a `clientResult`; a client error is an event and never ends the main session. The main script decides whether missing or failed client work matters.

`--raw` is live NDJSON with `started`, `ready`, `event`, `log`, `clientResult`, `capture`, `dropped`, `aborted`, and `result` records. Each physical line is independently valid JSON. Events are not deduplicated or sampled by the CLI; source rate limiting is visible through accurate `dropped` counts.

Inside a playscript, `playtest.capture(name)` and `playtest.clip(seconds, name)` record the client viewport mid-session and return `{ok, name, media}`. The bytes never travel through the run: each call emits a `capture` record and `playtest run` saves the file as `<name>.png` or `<name>.mp4` under `--capture-dir`. Names may use letters, digits, `-`, `_`, and `.` only. Both are PlayClient-only, a clip is capped at 30 seconds by Roblox, and a capture that cannot be saved warns without failing the run.

Runtime heartbeats distinguish quiet scripts from vanished jobs. Missing heartbeats cause a status confirmation before `aborted` is emitted, and every failure reports the final observed job status instead of an empty exec-style value.
Encoded main/client results are capped at 1 MiB. An oversized value is replaced by `{"truncated":true,"bytes":N}` with its original byte count; stream bulk telemetry through `emit` instead.

`--identity game` is the default and runs through a temporary Script/LocalScript in the disposable playtest clone. Plugin identity is an explicit escape hatch in the plugin sandbox and cannot require game modules.

All runtime changes are temporary and never sync to disk or persist to edit mode. Play and Run DataModels are a separate environment and never reverse-sync. Run coordination is authenticated with the private job generation token. The start audit record includes script paths and SHA-256 hashes; the completion record includes the outcome and exit code.

`start` returns a lower-level asynchronous job. Use `--wait`, `playtest wait`, `status`, and `contexts` to synchronize with `server` and `client:N`; the low-level commands remain supported and unchanged.

Runtime copies communicate only with the edit-mode plugin through PluginConnectionService. They do not connect to localhost. `playtest capture --context client:N -o FILE` writes one PNG and `playtest clip --context client:N --seconds 1-30 -o FILE` writes one MP4; both take a PlayClient context only, because the PlayServer renders no viewport. A running experience cannot read a screenshot back into pixels, so the engine writes each frame into Roblox's capture directory and the local CLI copies it out and deletes it — no screenshot permission is requested and no artifact is uploaded from Studio.

playtest exec accepts exactly one of --source, --source-file or --stdin; --source-file - also reads stdin. Leading Luau comments are accepted inline. --timeout for exec is 1-60 seconds (other playtest operations have separate bounds).
playtest exec prints the runtime value/count result and exits nonzero when the submitted source fails, even if delivery succeeded. Earlier source mutations may have applied before that error.

Existing-job operations accept --job <ID>: status, contexts, wait, exec, logs, ui, input, capture, clip, stop, and request. A stale generation cannot select or mutate a newer runtime. Pin the job returned by start when coordinating multiple agents. start itself creates a new generation and rejects --job.
wait --context client:1 waits for that exact context to be ready; a different ready context does not satisfy it. start --wait pins its own returned job ID.

Exec results always include count. Returns without nil use value (one value or a dense array); returns containing nil use results with indexed slots {index:1,value:...} or {index:2,isNil:true}. Each returned value is serialized once so ordinary results retain the full 1 MiB envelope capacity.

The exec source timeout is separate from its request deadline: WSync reserves an additional 45 seconds for dispatch and multipart result transfer, so a valid near-deadline script is not cut off while returning its result.

commands.name: run
commands.title: wsync run
commands.description: Validates and executes a versioned JSON workflow over one persistent daemon session with typed references, preconditions, transactions, assertions, waits, verification, and idempotent replay.
notes: Schema version 1 supports get, set, new, rm, mv, attr-set, attr-rm, attr-ls, tag-add, tag-rm, assert, wait, eval, capture, call, playtest, and upload steps.

A string containing exactly `$stepId.value.path` references an earlier result while preserving its JSON type; use `$$literal` to emit a string beginning with `$`. Forward, self, unknown, and missing-path references fail validation or execution precisely.

Declare contiguous atomic transaction groups and assign steps with `transaction`. Atomic groups use Studio change-history recording and cancel automatically on failure; eval, call, wait, capture, playtest, and upload are rejected inside atomic groups.
Use workflow/step `expectedMode`, `expectedPlaceId`, `expectedClass`, and `etag` preconditions to reject stale targets. Set `verify: true` on supported writes for read-back verification.
Assertions support equals, not-equals, exists, truthy, contains, and numeric comparisons. Wait polls one path/property until its assertion passes or `timeoutMs` expires.

A successful workflow with `idempotencyKey` is recorded under `.wsync-workflows/`; rerunning the same key returns the prior result with `replayed: true`. `--dry-run` validates and prints normalized dependencies without executing.

commands.name: plan
commands.title: wsync plan
commands.description: Builds a read-only JSON plan for a mutating command without executing it.
commands.usage:
wsync plan set --path <studio-path> --prop <property> --value <json>
wsync plan new --path <parent-path> --class <ClassName> [--name <Name>] [--props <json-object>]
wsync plan rm --path <studio-path>
wsync plan mv --from <studio-path> --to <parent-path> [--force]
wsync plan resolve --path <filesystem-path> (--disk | --studio)
examples: wsync plan new --path ReplicatedStorage --class Folder --name Shared
notes: Does not mutate disk or Studio.
Returns `mutates`, `requires`, `risks`, and an `executeCommand` string.
Available as a dry-run explanation before a risky write; it is not a mandatory ritual before every mutation.

commands.name: query
commands.title: wsync query
commands.description: Matches a selector inside Studio and optionally projects selected properties, attributes, and tags without downloading the full live tree.
notes: `*` matches one path segment and `**` matches zero or more segments.
Matching and projection run in Studio, making this preferable to requesting a deep full tree for broad searches.
Repeat `--prop` for only the properties you need; `--attributes` and `--tags` add those maps to each JSON match.

`--limit` defaults to 200 and accepts 1-10000. JSON output is `{matches,count,truncated,truncationReason,limit,visitedNodes,responseBytes}`; paths/classes are line formats and print a reason-specific warning to stderr when the result is truncated.
Selectors match instance names and paths, not classes. To find every RemoteEvent regardless of name, use `wsync find --class RemoteEvent --under ReplicatedStorage --raw`.

--raw aliases the default JSON format; do not combine it with --format. --props is an alias of --prop (repeat once per property). Inspect truncated/truncationReason before treating results as complete; narrow the subtree or explicitly raise --limit if needed.

commands.name: path
commands.title: wsync path
commands.description: Translates between Studio instance paths and syncable filesystem paths using the live Studio tree.
notes: Resolution runs through the project's sync rules, so any instance the middleware maps answers — scripts, value modules, `.model.json`/`.rbxm` subtrees, and `.data.json`-backed instances alike.
Instances outside the projection — not under a mapped root, excluded by `ignoreGlobs`, or inside an `AvoidSync` subtree — are reported as Studio-only instead of being given an invented path.
Generated files such as `wsync.md` are not syncable Studio instances.

commands.name: lint
commands.title: wsync lint
commands.description: Runs `luau-lsp analyze` with named Roblox definitions and selectable live-Studio or filesystem DataModel typing, then optionally compiles bytecode at every optimization level to catch compiler-only failures.
notes: The default `--data-model auto` mode merges the complete live Studio tree into disk script mappings and enables strict DataModel diagnostics when a matching daemon/plugin is connected; otherwise it reports a relaxed filesystem fallback.

`--data-model studio` requires that live full-DataModel strict check. `filesystem` performs a strict offline audit that may report false unknown children for Studio-only instances, while `loose` keeps filesystem DataModel expressions gradual.

Auto/studio discovery reaches the project's daemon through its route on the WSync hub; `--port` talks to a daemon's own port directly instead. `--raw` returns JSON diagnostics plus DataModel coverage, strictness, live-node count, analyzer status, and suppressed counts.

Without `--path`, default vendor ignores hide common dependency/tooling folders such as `Packages`, `_Index`, `Madwork*`, `PlayerModule`, `node_modules`, `tools`, `.git`, `.codex`, `.vscode`, and WSync's `.wsync-*` runtime/backup folders. Any explicit `--path` overrides those defaults so the requested target is never silently skipped.

`--scope-only` / `--owned-only` requires at least one `--path`, shows only diagnostics in those scopes, reports suppressed dependency diagnostics, and does not fail solely for diagnostics outside the requested scopes.

WSync injects bundled Roblox definitions as the named `@roblox` set. Extra named sets such as `--definitions:@testez=...` coexist; an explicit `--definitions:@roblox=...` after `--` replaces the bundled set.
WSync recommends luau-lsp 1.68.1 or newer. If `--luau-lsp` is omitted, it checks `WSYNC_LUAU_LSP`, bundled/Aftman locations, and then `PATH`.

The default `--compile auto` pass runs every in-scope executable script through `luau-compile --null` at `-O0`, `-O1`, and `-O2` when the compiler is available. It catches bytecode-generation failures such as the 200-local-register limit. Use `required` to fail when the compiler is unavailable or `off` to disable this pass.

Compiler resolution checks `--luau-compile`, `WSYNC_LUAU_COMPILE`, `LUAU_COMPILE`, the bundled platform tool, Aftman, and `PATH`. Raw JSON distinguishes analyzer and compiler diagnostics, includes compiler coverage/failure metadata, and preserves unparsed analyzer messages such as configuration errors.

Structured diagnostics recognize luau-lsp's default and GNU formatters, including adversarial Studio instance names. `--formatter=plain` is rejected because luau-lsp 1.68.1 can emit TypeErrors in that mode while returning a successful process status.
`--no-sourcemap` disables WSync DataModel coverage. Requiring `studio` or `filesystem` mode while disabling or replacing the generated sourcemap is rejected.
The narrowest `lint --path <file>` is the intended post-edit verification step; unrelated global diff output is not.

With an explicit --project, relative --path values are resolved against the selected project directory; absolute --path values remain absolute. Without --project, --path follows cwd. Tool and output file paths remain cwd-relative.

commands.name: upload
commands.title: wsync upload
commands.description: Uploads Roblox assets through Open Cloud from files or directories.
notes: Credentials resolve from the selected profile's key (`--profile` or `WSYNC_PROFILE`) first, then the `wsync auth` store, then the environment variable named by `--api-key-env`, then `ROBLOX_API_KEY`, `CLOUD_API_KEY`, and `ROBLOX_OPEN_CLOUD_API_KEY`.
The creator is `--creator`, else the selected profile's creator, else the project's `groupId`. A profile named but not stored is refused before any upload.
Directories recurse by default, skip unsupported files, and continue after per-file failures.
Use `--auth bearer` for OAuth tokens instead of API keys. `--no-wait` returns operation handles instead of polling each asset to completion.

`--grant-universe <id>` grants that experience permission to use every uploaded asset through the Open Cloud Asset Permissions API, so an asset owned by one account or group can be used in another's game; `--asset-id` (repeatable) grants existing assets without uploading. The key needs the `asset-permissions:write` scope. The API can answer 200 while refusing an asset, so only assets it lists as granted count; anything else, and `--no-wait` uploads that have no asset id yet, fails the command.

commands.name: monetization
commands.title: wsync monetization
commands.description: Discovers, lists, creates, edits, and uploads images for Roblox game passes and developer products through Open Cloud.
commands.usage:
wsync monetization gamepass discover [--project <path>]
wsync monetization gamepass list [--project <path>] [--universe-id <id>] [--api-key-env <name>] [--profile <name>] [--raw]
wsync monetization gamepass create [--project <path>] [--universe-id <id>] [--api-key-env <name>] [--profile <name>] [--description <text>] [--image <file>] [--not-for-sale] (<entry>... | --name <name> --price <robux>)
wsync monetization gamepass edit [--project <path>] [--universe-id <id>] [--api-key-env <name>] [--profile <name>] (--id <id> | --name <existing-name>) [--new-name <name>] [--price <robux>] [--description <text>] [--for-sale true|false]
wsync monetization gamepass image [--project <path>] [--universe-id <id>] [--api-key-env <name>] [--profile <name>] (--id <id> | --name <existing-name>) <file>
wsync monetization gamepass images [--project <path>] [--universe-id <id>] [--api-key-env <name>] [--profile <name>] <dir>
# Replace gamepass with product, dp, devproduct, gp, pass, or gamepasses as needed.
examples: wsync monetization product create "Coins Small 49 robux, Coins Large 399 robux" --project .
notes: Uses multipart/form-data and Roblox Open Cloud API keys.

Credential discovery checks the selected profile's key (`--profile` or `WSYNC_PROFILE`), then the `wsync auth` store, then `ROBLOX_API_KEY`, `CLOUD_API_KEY`, `ROBLOX_OPEN_CLOUD_API_KEY`, and project env files.
Universe discovery checks `--universe-id`, `ROBLOX_UNIVERSE_ID`, `UNIVERSE_ID`, `GAMEID`, `GAME_ID`, project env files, and then the `gameId` field in `default.project.json`.
`discover` reports likely monetization config files but does not guess project-specific code writes when the schema is ambiguous.
`images` matches files to assets by normalized filename, such as coins-small.png to Coins Small.

commands.name: get
commands.title: wsync get
commands.description: Reads an instance view or one property from the live Studio session.
notes: Requires the daemon and Studio plugin to be connected.
Reads the whole live DataModel, including instances the project does not project to disk.

commands.name: ls
commands.title: wsync ls
commands.description: Lists the direct children of a live Studio instance.
notes: An empty path lists top-level DataModel services.
Use `tree` when you need recursive output.

commands.name: tree
commands.title: wsync tree
commands.description: Prints a class and name tree below a live Studio instance.
notes: Depth defaults to 3; use 0 for only the root instance.

Covers the whole live DataModel. That is a superset of the project's disk projection, because instances outside the project tree, under `ignoreGlobs`, or inside an `AvoidSync` subtree exist in Studio only.
The live tree is authoritative. Prefer a bounded `--depth` over a wide dump; wide trees are a higher-token read.

commands.name: snapshot
commands.title: wsync snapshot
commands.description: Exports the live Studio tree plus inspectable properties, attributes, and tags to deterministic JSON.
notes: Defaults to `wsync-snapshot-<unix-seconds>.json` under the project or current directory.
The export covers the whole DataModel projection, not only script-backed instances, and uses the same tagged-value encoding as the sync protocol.
Backed by the daemon `/snapshot` route, which also serves subtree exports by ref.
This is a backup and debugging tool. It is the most expensive read in the CLI; reach for `tree`, `ls`, or `query` first.

commands.name: rbxl
commands.title: wsync rbxl
commands.description: Refreshes place.rbxl beside the project file: the connected Studio's whole place as a binary place file, for offline tools such as Lune.
notes: The file is always `place.rbxl` next to the project file. Open it from Lune with `roblox.deserializePlace(fs.readFile("place.rbxl"))`; run this command first when the script needs Studio's current state.

It is made from what Studio holds, not from disk, so Studio-only instances (parts, UI, models) are in it even in a code-scope project. Each service is serialized by Roblox SerializationService, so classes, properties, attributes, tags, scripts, and references within a service survive; references that cross services are dropped, and a service's own properties travel separately (refs excluded).

The daemon also refreshes the file in the background while Studio is connected: every `place_file_interval` seconds (default 300), never during a playtest or in the first 30 seconds of a connection. Set `place_file = false` in `wsync.toml` to turn the background refresh off; this command still works.

Only services that changed since their last capture are serialized again. Serializing freezes Studio while it runs (seconds for a very large service), so an unchanged place costs nothing and a first capture costs the most.
The write is atomic: a reader never sees a half-written file. When nothing is connected the command fails and says whether an older copy is on disk.
The daemon adds `place.rbxl` to the repository's `.git/info/exclude` when nothing ignores it yet, so a branch finish never commits it.

commands.name: backlog
commands.title: wsync backlog
commands.description: Reviews, restores, or drops the disk content that lost to Studio. WSync is Studio-first and never stops to ask: a connect applies Studio over the project and a mid-session clash resolves the same way, so the disk bytes that lost are moved to the backlog instead of being dropped or waiting behind a prompt.
notes: Sync is Studio-first with no questions asked. A connect applies Studio over the project, and a change that clashes with Studio mid-session resolves toward Studio the moment it is detected. Neither stops to ask, because being interrupted by a decision you did not plan to make is worse than the loss it guards against.

The guard is this backlog. Whenever disk content would be overwritten or dropped, its bytes move to `.wsync-backups/backlog/` first, recorded with the path they came from and whether they lost to the initial sync or to a later conflict.

`restore <id>` writes an entry back to its project path and pushes it to Studio, which is the old Keep Disk answer, deferred until you actually want it. It needs a connected Studio plugin: a restore that never reaches Studio would be sent straight back to the backlog by the next connect.

Entries expire a day after capture and are swept on every read, so an expiry never depends on the app being open. The backlog is a safety net for the edit you did not notice losing, not a version history.
`drop` forgets an entry without restoring it; `drop --all` empties the backlog. Neither touches what is already synced.

There is no divergence prompt, no pending review, and no Keep Disk / Keep Studio decision anywhere in WSync. The commands that drove them — `diff`, `changes`, `decision`, `conflicts`, and `resolve` — no longer exist.

commands.name: services
commands.title: wsync services
commands.description: Lists the project's sync roots and whether each exists on disk and in the live Studio DataModel.
notes: Roots come from the project file's `tree` and its `$path` mappings, not from a fixed service allowlist, so any service or nested instance the project maps is listed.
Each row reports the Studio path, the mapped project path, and presence on each side; this is the cheapest way to learn a project's sync scope.

commands.name: meta
commands.title: wsync meta
commands.description: Shows the Studio path, class, filesystem path, and existence status for a syncable path.
notes: Uses the live Studio tree; start `wsync serve --project .` and connect the Studio plugin first.
Resolves through the same middleware as `path`, so a sidecar-backed or model-backed instance reports every file that backs it, not just a script path.

commands.name: props
commands.title: wsync props
commands.description: Prints inspectable live Studio properties for one instance.
notes: This is a focused view over `wsync get --path <path>`.
`Ref`-typed and `SharedString` properties are not encodable and are omitted.

commands.name: source
commands.title: wsync source
commands.description: Prints an instance's script source from live Studio, or the content of the file backing it on disk.
notes: Without `--disk`, reads the live `Source` through the plugin's `ScriptEditorService` path. Live source is unreliable while an editor draft is open for that script, so a mismatch is not by itself proof of divergence.
`--disk` resolves the target through the sync middleware, so `.model.json`, `.rbxm`, and `.data.json`-backed instances answer as well as plain script files.
This is a loose divergence diagnostic, not a verification step. To verify an edit, use the narrowest `wsync lint --path` plus a local file read.

Prefer --output to shell redirection for saved source: it writes only after a successful string response, using an atomic replacement. A failed read leaves an existing destination untouched. --raw preserves structured diagnostics; do not merge stderr into saved source. Output paths are relative to cwd.

commands.name: where
commands.title: wsync where
commands.description: Finds live Studio instances by name substring and, when possible, resolves a target path to disk.
notes: Combines a live name search with middleware path translation when `--project` is supplied.
Matches that the project does not project to disk are still listed, marked Studio-only.

commands.name: open
commands.title: wsync open
commands.description: Opens a cloud place in Roblox Studio by place id, or selects one or more Studio instances by path.
notes: A single all-digit argument is a place id; anything else is a Studio path, so the two forms never collide.

The place form launches Studio through the `roblox-studio:` protocol URL (`task:EditPlace`), which needs both the place id and its universe; the universe is taken from a daemon that already claims the place, or from `--project`'s `gameId`, and is otherwise requested with `--universe`.

When no daemon serves the place, a scratch project is created under `<projectsRoot>/_places/<placeId>` and its daemon is started, so the place is addressable as soon as Studio connects; the scratch project deletes itself when Studio closes. `--keep` keeps it, `--into <dir>` puts it elsewhere (never auto-deleted), and `--no-attach` only launches Studio.
The path form is a shorthand over `wsync select set --paths '[...]'`.
With the `OpenInEditor` plugin setting on, selecting a script also opens it in the Studio script editor.

commands.name: launch
commands.title: wsync launch
commands.description: Launches Roblox Studio on a place given as either a place file on disk or a cloud place id, without creating a project or starting a daemon.
notes: An all-digit argument is a place id; anything else is a path to a .rbxl or .rbxlx file. A path that does not exist is tried with .rbxl and .rbxlx appended when smart paths are on, the way wsync studio resolves one; a file that is still missing is an error, never a place id.

A place id launches Studio through the roblox-studio: protocol URL (task:EditPlace), which needs the universe too: --universe, else a daemon on this machine that already claims the place, else --project's gameId. Nothing is attached: no scratch project is created and no daemon is started. Use wsync open for a place that should be addressable as soon as Studio connects, and wsync studio to launch Studio with no place.

Launching returns before the place has finished loading. --raw prints {"ok": true, "launched": true, "pid": <n>} with either "file" or "placeId", "universeId" and "url"; the pid is the process that was spawned, and Studio may re-exec itself into another.

commands.name: places
commands.title: wsync places
commands.description: Lists every WSync daemon with the places it serves, its port, branch, and whether a Studio plugin is connected.
notes: Reads the WSync hub's `GET /daemons` (every registered daemon with its live `/hello`, docs/hub.md), then the runtime records under the state directory; nothing is started, stopped, or written.

A record whose daemon is not registered with the hub is still listed as `unreachable`, with the place ids its project file claims, so a stale record is visible rather than silent. A daemon from a build that predates the hub appears this way until it is restarted.
The `KIND` column marks scratch projects created by `wsync open <placeId>`: `attach` for one that persists, `attach (ephemeral)` for one that deletes itself when Studio closes.
Place ids listed here are what the global `--place <placeId>` option resolves against.

commands.name: tail
commands.title: wsync tail
commands.description: Streams Studio output, warning, and error messages until interrupted.
notes: Equivalent to `wsync logs --tail`.

commands.name: watch
commands.title: wsync watch
commands.description: Streams raw daemon WebSocket frames for debugging sync traffic.
notes: Connects to the daemon WebSocket as a watch-role client and prints received event/lifecycle frames. Protocol heartbeat ping/pong messages are handled internally.

Without --port, it connects through the project's route on the WSync hub (`ws://127.0.0.1:7960/p/<route>/ws`, docs/hub.md); --port connects to a daemon's own port instead. --project and the positional project are alternatives.
--raw suppresses the status banner and prints NDJSON frames. --compact prints one-line human summaries; combining it with --raw still selects summaries.
Use this for daemon/plugin events; wsync logs or wsync tail are the tools for Studio output.

commands.name: repair
commands.title: wsync repair
commands.description: Checks live tree access and rebuilds generated WSync metadata.
commands.usage:
wsync repair tree [--project <path>] [--port <port>] [--depth <n>] [--raw]
wsync repair sourcemap [--project <path>] [--output <path>] [--raw]
notes: `repair tree` validates that the live Studio tree can be read; use `wsync tree` or `wsync query` to inspect it.

`repair sourcemap` rebuilds a luau-lsp sourcemap from the project's on-disk tree and is the recovery path when the generated file is missing or stale. `wsync sourcemap` is the primary command and can also watch.

commands.name: find
commands.title: wsync find
commands.description: Finds live Studio instances by class name and/or name substring.
notes: Omit `--under` to search the whole DataModel.
An unbounded search is a higher-token read; scope it with `--under` when the parent is known.

commands.name: find-attr
commands.title: wsync find-attr
commands.description: Finds live Studio instances that have a named attribute, optionally matching a value.
notes: `--value` uses the same JSON literal and tagged-value codec as `wsync set --value`.

Offline value schemas and copyable examples for every supported type: `wsync commands types`; narrow with `wsync commands types Vector3` or `wsync commands types Color3`. The live JSON wire format uses the exact `__type` key and lowercase component fields; arrays, constructor strings, and sidecar `{Vector3:[...]}` shapes are not equivalent.
Codec support does not imply attribute compatibility: Roblox SetAttribute supports only its attribute datatypes. Instance references, buffers, and output-only markers are not valid attribute values.

commands.name: classinfo
commands.title: wsync classinfo
commands.description: Lists properties and methods for a Roblox class using Studio reflection when available.
notes: Falls back to a baked table for common classes when reflection is unavailable.

commands.name: enums
commands.title: wsync enums
commands.description: Lists every Enum type name exposed by the connected Studio session.
notes: Use `wsync enum --name <EnumName>` to inspect one enum's items.

commands.name: enum
commands.title: wsync enum
commands.description: Lists the items for one Roblox Enum type.
notes: Outputs item names and underlying integer values.

commands.name: logs
commands.title: wsync logs
commands.description: Reads recent Studio output, warning, and error messages from the plugin log buffer.
notes: `--tail` streams until interrupted.
Always bound this with `--limit` or `--since`; an unbounded read is a higher-token command.

commands.name: status
commands.title: wsync status
commands.description: Summarizes daemon reachability, plugin handshake, project config, sourcemap, and write-log health.
notes: Use when the task needs current daemon/plugin health or a failed live operation needs diagnosis. Existing fresh context often makes another status call unnecessary; there is no mandatory context/status startup pair.

commands.name: doctor
commands.title: wsync doctor
commands.description: Runs a broader health check over project files, daemon, plugin, linter, and sourcemap setup.
notes: Use after `status` when setup or connectivity looks suspicious.

commands.name: ping
commands.title: wsync ping
commands.description: Round-trips a lightweight request to the Studio plugin and reports latency.
notes: A fast way to confirm the plugin WebSocket path is alive.

commands.name: version
commands.title: wsync version
commands.description: Prints the daemon version and build identity and, when reachable, the plugin version.
notes: Human and raw output include the daemon build commit and dirty state. The connected plugin reports its own build identity in the nested version response.
Binary, plugin, protocol number, and generated docs are released from one commit; a mismatch reported here means an unreleased or mixed install.

commands.name: refresh
commands.title: wsync refresh
commands.description: Refreshes generated WSync agent docs without starting the daemon.
notes: Updates `wsync.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `.codex/config.toml` while preserving project notes outside the generated marker blocks. Marker blocks owned by other tools are left untouched.
The generated docs also regenerate automatically on every plugin connect.
AGENTS.md contains a concise generated contract (at most 8 KiB) linking the detailed wsync.md project reference. Actual project mappings and active sync rules remain in that reference.
User notes and foreign marker blocks are preserved. Oversized AGENTS.md files trigger an instruction-budget warning; WSync never truncates notes. `wsync context` exposes size and warning metadata.

commands.name: set
commands.title: wsync set
commands.description: Sets one property or applies a batch of property writes in the live Studio session.
notes: Every successful write is appended to `writes.log`.
`set Parent` is refused by default; use `wsync mv`, or pass `--force-parent` only when raw parent assignment is intentional.
A `--batch` entry setting `Parent` rejects the whole batch before any request is made, with no escape — batches have no `--force-parent`; reparent with `wsync mv` or a single forced `set`.

A `Name` write whose value is empty or contains `/` is refused (single writes pre-network, a `--batch` entry rejects the whole file): paths are `/`-separated with no escaping, so such a name could never be addressed by a path-based command again.
`--waypoint` brackets the write so one Studio undo can reverse the batch.
`--batch` rejects the whole batch before any network call when any entry trips a guardrail; `--keep-going` only relaxes per-entry runtime failures, never the pre-flight guards.
Live mutating commands are user-initiated escape hatches. Inspect the exact live target with read-only commands and confirm intent before running one.

Offline value schemas and copyable examples for every supported type: `wsync commands types`; narrow with `wsync commands types Vector3` or `wsync commands types Color3`. The live JSON wire format uses the exact `__type` key and lowercase component fields; arrays, constructor strings, and sidecar `{Vector3:[...]}` shapes are not equivalent.
Color3 r/g/b use the 0–1 scale, not 0–255. For RGB(255,128,0), use {"__type":"Color3","r":1,"g":0.5019607843137255,"b":0}. Vector3 uses {"__type":"Vector3","x":1,"y":2,"z":3}.

Content has no JSON input tag: use native `Content.fromUri(...)` in `eval`/`exec` for Content properties, or an available legacy string property. Native Roblox datatype globals are already available there; no extra sandbox permission is needed for Vector3/Color3/CFrame constructors.

commands.name: new
commands.title: wsync new
commands.description: Creates a new live Studio instance under a parent path.
notes: `--props` uses the same value codec as `wsync set --value`.

`--name` (and a `Name` in `--props`) must not be empty or contain `/`: paths are `/`-separated with no escaping, so such a name could never be addressed by a path-based command. The refusal happens before any request is made, and the plugin refuses the same write again.
The created instance is written to `writes.log`.

If the parent is inside the project's projection, the new instance syncs back to disk through the write middleware; a leaf class with no dedicated middleware becomes a folder plus `.data.json`, or a `<Name>.model.json` when `syncback_model_json` is enabled.

Offline value schemas and copyable examples for every supported type: `wsync commands types`; narrow with `wsync commands types Vector3` or `wsync commands types Color3`. The live JSON wire format uses the exact `__type` key and lowercase component fields; arrays, constructor strings, and sidecar `{Vector3:[...]}` shapes are not equivalent.
Color3 r/g/b use the 0–1 scale, not 0–255. For RGB(255,128,0), use {"__type":"Color3","r":1,"g":0.5019607843137255,"b":0}. Vector3 uses {"__type":"Vector3","x":1,"y":2,"z":3}.

Content has no JSON input tag: use native `Content.fromUri(...)` in `eval`/`exec` for Content properties, or an available legacy string property. Native Roblox datatype globals are already available there; no extra sandbox permission is needed for Vector3/Color3/CFrame constructors.

commands.name: rm
commands.title: wsync rm
commands.description: Destroys a live Studio instance.
notes: Calls `:Destroy()` through the plugin and records the write in `writes.log`.
Deletions that reach disk through syncback honor `move_to_bin`; force-overwrite and prune paths back removed trees up to `.wsync-backups/<timestamp>/` first.

commands.name: mv
commands.title: wsync mv
commands.description: Reparents a live Studio instance to a destination parent path.
notes: Cross-service moves require `--force` to catch accidental DataModel reshuffles.
Use this instead of `wsync set --prop Parent`.
A reparent reaches disk as a remove plus an add, so file history does not follow the move.

commands.name: attr
commands.title: wsync attr
commands.description: Lists, sets, or removes attributes on a live Studio instance.
notes: `attr ls` is read-only; `attr set` and `attr rm` are written to `writes.log`.
`--value` uses the same JSON literal and tagged-value codec as `wsync set --value`.

Attributes on projected instances sync back to their `.data.json` sidecar. Setting the boolean `AvoidSync` attribute to `true` keeps that instance and its subtree in Studio: the plugin pushes a removal (its files leave disk, as for a deletion in Studio), and from then on nothing under it is written to disk, pushed over from disk, or counted by the connect-time comparison. Removing the attribute syncs the subtree back. The daemon never reads the attribute from a sidecar; a disk-side exclusion is `ignoreGlobs`.

Offline value schemas and copyable examples for every supported type: `wsync commands types`; narrow with `wsync commands types Vector3` or `wsync commands types Color3`. The live JSON wire format uses the exact `__type` key and lowercase component fields; arrays, constructor strings, and sidecar `{Vector3:[...]}` shapes are not equivalent.
Color3 r/g/b use the 0–1 scale, not 0–255. For RGB(255,128,0), use {"__type":"Color3","r":1,"g":0.5019607843137255,"b":0}. Vector3 uses {"__type":"Vector3","x":1,"y":2,"z":3}.
Codec support does not imply attribute compatibility: Roblox SetAttribute supports only its attribute datatypes. Instance references, buffers, and output-only markers are not valid attribute values.

commands.name: tag
commands.title: wsync tag
commands.description: Adds or removes CollectionService tags on a live Studio instance.
notes: Successful tag mutations are written to `writes.log`.
Tags on projected instances sync back to their `.data.json` sidecar.

commands.name: call
commands.title: wsync call
commands.description: Invokes a method on a live Studio instance and prints the returned value.
notes: `--args` is a JSON array using the same tagged-value codec as `wsync set --value`.
Treat methods with side effects as writes; successful calls are audited.

Offline value schemas and copyable examples for every supported type: `wsync commands types`; narrow with `wsync commands types Vector3` or `wsync commands types Color3`. The live JSON wire format uses the exact `__type` key and lowercase component fields; arrays, constructor strings, and sidecar `{Vector3:[...]}` shapes are not equivalent.

Content has no JSON input tag: use native `Content.fromUri(...)` in `eval`/`exec` for Content properties, or an available legacy string property. Native Roblox datatype globals are already available there; no extra sandbox permission is needed for Vector3/Color3/CFrame constructors.

commands.name: select
commands.title: wsync select
commands.description: Reads or replaces the current Studio Selection.
notes: `select get` is read-only; `select set` is a Studio state change.
Selection payloads are chunked; very large selections page rather than arriving in one frame.

commands.name: copy
commands.title: wsync copy
commands.description: Copies arbitrary native Studio instance trees into WSync's private cross-project clipboard.
notes: With no paths, copies the current Studio Explorer selection.
Roblox SerializationService preserves native instance types, descendants, properties, attributes, tags, scripts, and references among roots copied together.
The private clipboard is shared across WSync projects and survives CLI process exit; a successful copy atomically replaces it.
Services cannot be copied. References to instances outside the copied roots cannot cross places, matching native Studio behavior.
Bounded at 256 roots and 128 MiB per copy.

commands.name: paste
commands.title: wsync paste
commands.description: Pastes WSync's native instance clipboard into the connected Studio as one undoable change.
notes: Without `--to`, every copied root returns to its recorded class/name/ordinal parent route in the destination place, including paths with `/` in a name and duplicate same-named siblings.
Use `--to` (alias `--parent`) when the original parent hierarchy does not exist in the destination.
Pasted roots are selected by default. One Studio Undo removes the full paste.
Paste is reusable: it does not consume the private clipboard.

commands.name: eval
commands.title: wsync eval
commands.description: Executes Luau source inside Studio through the plugin sandbox and returns the result.
notes: Use `return ...` when you need a returned value. Native Roblox globals such as Vector3.new, Color3.fromRGB, CFrame.new, UDim2.new, Enum, and Instance.new are available in Studio execution; the JSON wire tags are for set/new/attr/call arguments. Discover them offline with `wsync commands types`.

Choose exactly one source input. `--source-file -` also reads stdin. Source file paths are relative to the shell working directory. Leading comments (including --!strict) are accepted by --source; file/stdin avoids shell quoting and argument length limits.
`eval` is request/response against one connected Studio session and carries the standard 5 second remote-op timeout. `wsync exec` is the fire-and-forget broadcast form and acknowledges queuing only.
Use within the user-authorized task scope. A timeout or execution/encoding failure can follow earlier mutations; inspect affected state before retrying, and use the operation receipt when provided.

commands.name: transmit
commands.title: wsync transmit
commands.description: Runs an optional Studio render script, reads EditableImage/ImageLabel/ImageButton/MeshPart texture pixels from Studio, and writes local PNG files for editing or upload.
notes: The plugin accepts EditableImage objects directly and can also read ImageLabel/ImageButton content through AssetService.
Use `wsync capture ui`, `capture model`, or `capture viewport` to create permission-free PNGs through WSync's internal RGBA renderer.

MeshParts with object-backed TextureContent are supported. WSync reads Content.Object directly when it is already an EditableImage, otherwise it falls back to CreateEditableImageAsync for TextureContent or TextureID.

`--source` and `--source-file` execute with loadstring in the plugin's real Studio environment, so normal globals like game, workspace, require, Rect, and Vector2 are available without a custom sandbox.
Large batches are prepared once, then downloaded one image per request so full 768x768 render sets do not have to fit in one WebSocket response.

If `--source` or `--source-file` returns images, those are captured. If `--from` is supplied, WSync also walks that Studio subtree after the source runs and captures any image-like instances found there.
The command writes PNG files locally. Use `wsync upload` afterwards when you want to publish the edited images to Roblox Open Cloud.
This executes Luau in Studio, so treat it like `wsync eval`: inspect render scripts first and avoid destructive code.

commands.name: waypoint
commands.title: wsync waypoint
commands.description: Creates a named Studio change-history waypoint.
notes: Use waypoints before and after multi-step edits so Studio undo has a clear boundary.
Every applied sync batch already creates its own named waypoint, so a manual waypoint marks agent-driven work specifically.

commands.name: undo
commands.title: wsync undo
commands.description: Requests Studio to undo one change-history entry.
notes: Pairs naturally with `--waypoint` on `wsync set` for reversible batches.
A completed bulk disk-to-Studio pull is one recording, so one undo reverses the whole pull.

commands.name: redo
commands.title: wsync redo
commands.description: Requests Studio to redo the last undone change-history entry.
notes: Requires the same live Studio/plugin connection as `undo`.

commands.name: serve
commands.title: wsync serve
commands.description: Runs a local HTTP/WebSocket server with filesystem watching, optionally in an asynchronous child process.
notes: Runs in the foreground unless --async or the run_async configuration is enabled. --async spawns a WSync child process.
--project is the named alternative to the positional project. Use the positional form when also supplying a session identifier; both project forms together are rejected.

The host comes from --host, then the project, then configuration. The port comes from --port, then the project file's `port`; with neither, the OS hands out a free one. A pinned port that is taken is an error — nothing scans for another. Either way the server registers with the WSync hub on 127.0.0.1:7960 (starting one if none answers), so Studio and the CLI reach it at its project route `/p/<route>` whatever port it bound. The process registers the port it actually bound in ~/.wsync/sessions.toml for wsync stop.
--sourcemap keeps sourcemap.json regenerated from the live tree. --ts enables the roblox-ts watcher.

For the project lifecycle record and manager authentication, use wsync daemon start. That command also stays in the current process while serving; launch it through your process manager when background operation is needed.
Serve does not accept game/group/place metadata flags. Configure project metadata in the project file or use wsync daemon start --game-id/--group-id/--place-id.

commands.name: build
commands.title: wsync build
commands.description: Serializes the project tree into a Roblox place or model file, optionally rebuilding on every change.
notes: Requires a project. It builds from the in-memory tree with no filesystem rescan and never starts, contacts, or requires a daemon or the Studio plugin.
A `DataModel` root produces a place (`.rbxl`, or `.rbxlx` with `--xml`); any other root produces a model (`.rbxm`, or `.rbxmx` with `--xml`). An explicit `--output` extension wins over `--xml`.
`--plugin` writes the built model into the local Roblox Studio plugins directory instead of the project, which is how a `plugin` template is tested.
`--watch` stays in the foreground and rebuilds off the internal change bus; add `--sourcemap` to keep the sourcemap regenerated alongside each build.
`--ts` enables the roblox-ts passthrough for TypeScript projects.
The output is a build artifact, not a sync surface: writing it back into the project does not push anything to Studio.
--project and the positional project path are alternatives; supplying both is an error. Output file paths stay relative to cwd.

commands.name: sourcemap
commands.title: wsync sourcemap
commands.description: Writes a JSON sourcemap of the project tree, optionally regenerating it every time a file changes.
notes: The project is taken from the positional argument or from --project; the two are mutually exclusive. It defaults to the current directory.
Without --output the sourcemap is written to sourcemap.json beside the project file. A directory or extension-less path is completed to sourcemap.json inside it when smart paths are enabled.
--watch keeps the process running and rewrites the sourcemap on every change; --async (-A) detaches that watcher into a background child.
--non-scripts includes instances that carry no script source, which the default output omits.

commands.name: exec
commands.title: wsync exec
commands.description: Broadcasts Luau source to every connected Studio client and returns immediately.
notes: Requires the daemon and at least one connected Studio plugin. Safety: mutates Studio — the source runs at the plugin's trust level, exactly like `wsync eval`.
The argument is Luau source, or a path to a `.luau`/`.lua` file whose contents are sent.

`exec` is fire-and-forget: the daemon delivers one `execute` frame to every connected client and no value comes back. `wsync eval` is the request/response form and is what to use when the result matters.
Because it broadcasts, every connected place runs the code. Scope work with `wsync eval` when only one session should be touched.
`--focus` raises the Roblox Studio window before the code runs.
With --project, the daemon identity must match the canonical project and boot; --port never overrides that check. Legacy positional session/--host targeting remains available.

Success acknowledges that the daemon queued the broadcast. It does not prove the code ran or completed. HTTP/transport failures exit nonzero; a lost reply may follow execution, so inspect state before retrying. --raw exposes queued and completion:unknown.
Use within existing task authorization. --standalone fails explicitly and points to playtest run; it is not implemented.

commands.name: studio
commands.title: wsync studio
commands.description: Launches Roblox Studio, optionally opening a place/model file, with an option to reuse an already running Studio.
notes: Controls the local Studio application; no project, daemon or plugin connection is required.
With no path it launches Studio without a place file; a path opens that file.

--check means launch only when Studio is not already running. When Studio is running it reports that fact and exits successfully; when Studio is absent it launches Studio. This is not a read-only process-status query.
Launching returns before the place has finished loading. The plugin performs its own connection handshake afterwards.

--raw prints `{"pid": <n>}` for a launch, or `{"ok": true, "launched": false, "running": true}` when --check found Studio already running. The pid is the process that was spawned; Studio may re-exec itself, so it identifies the launch, not the window.

commands.name: debug
commands.title: wsync debug
commands.description: Drives Studio's play controls through keystroke automation.
notes: Defaults to `play`. `play` starts a playtest with a character, `run` runs the place without one, `start` starts a local server plus one client, and `stop` ends the current session.
Implemented as keyboard shortcuts sent to Studio; macOS and Windows only, and Studio must be running and frontmost. On macOS the calling application needs Accessibility permission.
Requires the Studio application, not a daemon or plugin connection. It reports what it sent, not what Studio did — there is no confirmation channel.
For scripted, observable playtests with return values, streamed logs, virtual input, and captures, use `wsync playtest` instead.
Runtime changes made during a debug session never sync to disk.

commands.name: stop
commands.title: wsync stop
commands.description: Stops running WSync sessions recorded in the global sessions file.
notes: Sessions are the `serve` and daemon entries registered in `~/.wsync/sessions.toml` as id to pid, host, and port. The port is the one each process actually bound, which the OS picks unless it was pinned; `--list` shows it.
With no arguments the last started session is stopped. `--all` stops every session, `--list` prints them and stops nothing, and `-H`/`-P` select sessions by address.
Mutates local daemon processes only. It never writes to the project, never touches Studio, and never resolves a pending conflict or divergence choice.

Shutdown goes through the daemon's authenticated `/stop` route. A PID read from a stale session or runtime record is never authority to kill a process; unreachable entries are pruned and reported instead.
`wsync daemon stop --project <path>` is the per-project form and matches the exact canonical project plus boot ID.
The WSync hub is not a session and `stop` leaves it alone; it exits on its own a minute after nothing is registered with it.

commands.name: update
commands.title: wsync update
commands.description: Updates selected WSync components: CLI/plugin from releases and templates from the embedded bundle.
notes: Default mode is all: it updates the CLI and includes the plugin/templates according to install_plugin and update_templates configuration. Explicit plugin or templates mode selects that component regardless of those all-mode switches.
CLI and plugin updates request GitHub releases. Template updates use the templates embedded in this CLI and do not need a release download.
--force bypasses WSync version guards and attempts the selected updates even when recorded versions appear current. Version bookkeeping is stored in ~/.wsync/update.toml.
Update output is human-readable; --raw is not implemented. Studio must reload the changed plugin file or restart before using it.
Use a matching CLI/plugin build when the protocol changes. An update command is an explicit mutation, not an offline version check.

commands.name: install
commands.title: wsync install
commands.description: Installs the running WSync binary to `~/.wsync/bin` and adds it to PATH, behind an explicit prompt.
notes: Writes only to `~/.wsync/bin` and shell PATH configuration; requires no daemon, project, or Studio.
Prompts before installing. Non-interactive runs are refused unless the global `-y` flag is passed.
The binary it was invoked from is never deleted or moved. This command replaces the removed first-run auto-installer, which could delete the invoked binary in non-interactive shells.
A package-managed binary (Homebrew, cargo install, and similar) is refused; use the package manager's own upgrade path instead.
`wsync update cli` keeps a self-installed binary current afterwards.

commands.name: config
commands.title: wsync config
commands.description: Reads, writes, lists, or restores WSync configuration values across the global and workspace layers.
notes: The global config is `~/.wsync/config.toml`; the workspace config is `wsync.toml` beside the project. Workspace beats global beats built-in defaults, and unset keys inherit rather than reset.
`--list` prints every setting with its current value, its default, and the doc comment that describes it. This is the authoritative option reference.
`-c global|workspace` selects the layer written; without it a set writes the global config.
`--default` restores the named setting to its built-in value, or every setting when no name is given.
`--export <path>` writes the fully resolved configuration (defaults merged with global and workspace overrides) to the given file instead of reading or writing a single key.
Unknown setting names and values that fail the setting's type are rejected before anything is written.

WSync-specific settings beyond the inherited set are `syncback_model_json` (false), `conflict_engine` (true), `compat_argon` (false), and `auto_open_app_modal` (true). `share_stats` defaults to false — telemetry is strictly opt-in.

There is no port setting: `port`, `scan_ports` and `port_scan_max` were removed when daemons moved behind the WSync hub (`127.0.0.1:7960`, `WSYNC_HUB_PORT` overrides). A daemon binds whatever port the OS hands out unless `--port` or the project file's `port` pins one. `wsync config` rejects the old names as unknown settings; a config file that still sets them loads normally and the keys are ignored.

commands.name: doc
commands.title: wsync doc
commands.description: Opens the WSync documentation site in the default browser.
notes: Opens https://github.com/Pugbread/wsync with the system browser and prints the URL. Browser launch failure is a command error.
For offline command documentation without opening a browser, use wsync commands <command>, wsync commands --compact, or wsync commands types.
